newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi says coalition stronger after local polls.
newsitem.headline: Prodi says coalition stronger after local polls.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Tuesday that the forces supporting his coaltion emerged strengthened by Italy's weekend local elections.
"The coalition that supports the government is stronger than before," he told reporters during a visit to southern Italy.

The coalition suffered a setback in the big cities of Milan and Turin, where centre-left candidates trailed in the first round of Sunday's elections and will have to challenge centre-right mayoral hopefuls in the May 11 run-offs.
But the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), the largest party in Prodi's coalition, did well overall in other mayoral races around the country.
Communist Refoundation, which is not part of the coalition but provides its margin of control in the lower house of parliament, did particularly well in races for provincial presidents.
In Milan, Turin and several other smaller municipalities the centre-left may need Communist Refoundation's help to beat the centre-right leaders in the run-offs.
Party leader Fausto Bertinotti indicated the political price could be high but Prodi said no single party emerged victorious form the polls.
"Communist Refoundation did not win," Prodi said. "The governing coalition won in an extremely difficult situation."

Prodi said the oppostion centre-right Freedom Alliance of former Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi was "mistaken" to think that the results meant a weakening of the coalition. -- Rome bureau +396-6782501
